chapter: Learning drums and Roy Eldridge's band
title: Roy's band: personnel, Eldridge Brothers 12 Rhythm Kings
summary: The band's size and instrumentation, its cabaret hours and name, and pianist George Hornsby playing with them.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah.
Yeah. So just think back to that band of Roy's.
Uh-huh.
How many guys -- you say two Buicks the guys travelled with.
Yeah.
So how many guys were there?
Well, let's see, we had -- let's see, there was Joe, unintelligible, and we had four saxes --
How did all those guys get in two Buicks?
Yeah, with the drums on the top.
Oh, my gosh. Well, who else? There's four saxophones.
And we had one trombone and three trumpets.
Who were the three trumpets? Roy and --
Roy and two more trumpet players.
Boy, that must have been a marvelous band, wasn't it?
It was a good band. We played -- we played, I guess we started around 9:00 and we finished at 5:00 o'clock in the morning. Every night.
(Laughter)
You mean on the road?
We played shows -- no, we were in this cabaret and then we went out. After we finished this cabaret. We stayed there a couple of months and then we went out on the road.
What was the name of the cabaret?
Oh, God, that's another problem.
All right.
But I'll think of it. I'll think of it.
That's it.
It was the Roy -- the Eldridge Brothers 12 Rhythm Kings, that was the name of the band.
Oh, that was the name that band had.
Uh-huh.
Fancy that. Well, so there was Frank on bass and yourself on drums. Did you use a guitar player?
No.
No. In those days people usually did, didn't they?
Yeah. We had this fellow, George Hornsby, was playing piano with us, when I come to think of it.
Oh, he was?
Yeah.
Before he went to church?
Yeah, before he went religious. Yeah.
You mean he left his own band?
Yeah. Because his band was just like a bunch of students, you know, and guys who had jobs and had day jobs. It was kind of a band, you know, just to -- I don't -- you know, kind of an amateur band.
Yes.
You know.
Yes.
These guys had jobs and --
Well, he must have had a big thrill working with a man like --
Well, it was a good band.
How about that.
Then we used to do --
